top.line: The next stage is a CRM of our own, on vaults, with an iOS app, for us and for our agents.
top.para: The field researched, ideas borrowed, and two teams: one builds, one uses.

in-short.line: Critical now; pieces exist; use it on ourselves; a fleet is a CRM; build the record; two teams.

ourselves.line: Build it by using it on our own team and agents first: managing a fleet of agents is relationship management.
ourselves.para: Agents as contacts, lanes as interactions, hand-overs as introductions; synthetic users answer emails.

why.line: After Web Summit, many follow-ups, messages and introductions, and no single place for them.
why.para: The fourth or fifth CRM, and the one that has to stick.

pieces.line: Vaults in the iOS app, image uploads, Apple Intelligence, a lane to the developers, keys, drafted outreach.
pieces.para: A CRM is a product with an iOS app of its own.

landscape.line: Twenty leads open source; Atomic and Relaticle are agent-friendly; commercial agentic CRMs propose and draft.
landscape.para: None records what each agent did.

plan.line: Build the record on vaults; borrow proposals, drafts, keys per agent, sources, first-class introductions.
plan.para: Twenty as reference and optional interface.

teams.line: A team develops the CRM; an agentic team captures, tidies, plans and drafts; only a person sends.
teams.para: Policies written by the ABP specialist.

next.line: Our own fleet first, then format and import, the pipeline, the iOS app, the Twenty sync, the product.

limits.line: A plan; a research snapshot; approval claims mostly the vendors' own.

sources.line: A research review of open-source and agentic CRMs, and earlier articles.
